scenes.narration: Every support team knows this sentence.
We couldn't reproduce it. It's where bug reports go to die. Customers wait. Support guesses. Engineering never sees the bug.
So we built an agent that doesn't guess. Introducing Show, Don't Tell. Built on TrueForge.
It starts where your team already works. A real ticket in Linear: a customer can't check out on their phone. On a laptop, everything looks fine.
The agent picks it up inside TrueForge. It lays out a plan, then reads the code in TrueForge's sandbox, and forms a hypothesis before it touches anything.
Then it proves it. It writes a browser check for what the customer expects, and runs it in an isolated browser lab. Desktop passes. On a phone, it fails. Reproduced.
It fixes the code, and runs the exact same check on a fresh copy of the app. Now it passes. A vision model confirms it independently. Before, and after. Proof, not a promise.
And anything you can't undo waits for a human. TrueForge holds the pull request, and the customer reply, until you approve.
One click, and the pull request lands on GitHub, with the video and a full verification record inside.
Approve the reply, and the customer gets what they actually needed: a video of their bug, fixed.
When it can't reproduce a bug, it says so honestly, and asks one precise question. And when a ticket tries to hijack it, it refuses, and flags it.
It doesn't even need to be asked. A TrueForge schedule sweeps your queue every hour, triages it, and takes the oldest bug. Autonomy, with a human on the leash.

Under the hood, it's all TrueForge. The sandbox, skills, MCP connectors for Linear, GitHub and our browser lab, tool approvals, generative UI, schedules and sessions. Open source, and one command to run.
Show, Don't Tell. Tickets in. Proof out. Built on TrueForge.
